results.enablePeerAccess_rc: 101 (hipErrorNotSupported - yet the peer copy still corrupted)

interpretation: Under amd_iommu=off, UNENABLED peer copies are CLEAN in both directions (hipMemcpyPeerAsync host-stages). Corruption appears only after a failed hipDeviceEnablePeerAccess( rc=101 ) - i.e. if an engine calls enable and ignores the error, subsequent copies in the dGPU->iGPU direction corrupt. This matches the handoff R4 (dev0->dev1 silent garbage) and implies llama.cpp/exllamav3 engines that call enablePeerAccess are the corrupt ones; engines that never enable (or check rc) are safe.
implication_for_multidevice: The fix may be simpler than amd_iommu: ensure engines do NOT call hipDeviceEnablePeerAccess, or ROCm fixes rc=101 handling. amd_iommu=off also removes the IOMMU variable entirely for future tests.
